items.q: Expand **MRP**.
items.explain: **MRP = Material Requirement Planning.** Do not mix it with **MRP II = Manufacturing Resource Planning** — *both* words change between the two, which is exactly the widening from *what parts do I need* to *what resources does the whole plant need*.

items.q: Expand **SCM**.
items.explain: **Supply Chain Management** — the oversight of **materials, information and finances** moving from supplier → manufacturer → wholesaler → retailer → consumer. The **S** of the **SPACES** mnemonic.

items.q: Expand **PLM**.
items.explain: **Product Lifecycle Management** — manages all data about a product **from initial conception to retirement**. Its curve has four stages: **Introduction → Growth → Maturity → Decline**.

items.q: Expand **BPR**.
items.explain: **Business Process Re-engineering** — it is what brought in the **'process view'** by the 1990s, and it is an activity inside the **Business Blueprinting** phase, sitting between the As-Is model and the To-Be process.

items.q: Expand **ASAP**.
items.explain: **Accelerated SAP** — SAP's own implementation methodology roadmap. Its five objectives: **Quick and cost effective · Maximize resource utilization · Involve users · Process oriented · Re-usability**.

items.q: **True or False:** Closed loop MRP checks feasibility of the MRP plan.
items.explain: **True.** Plain MRP **does not consider available capacity**, so its plan may be impossible. **Closed-loop MRP validates the plan, compares it with reality, checks feasibility and raises alerts/triggers** to the planner.

items.q: **True or False:** Enterprise application is a subset of ERP.
items.explain: **False — it is the other way round.** **ERP is a subset of Enterprise Business Systems**, albeit a large one that *'covers all the basic transactions inside the organization and dictates the overall business framework.'* EBS is the family; ERP is a member.

items.q: **True or False:** Project charter is a deliverable of the Business Blueprinting phase.
items.explain: **False.** The **project charter is a deliverable of Project Preparation (Phase 2).** Business Blueprinting delivers the **As-Is model, detailed requirements, gap document and To-Be process** — no charter.

items.q: **True or False:** In Big Bang, all ERP modules are implemented at selected locations.
items.explain: **False.** **Big Bang = all modules at ALL locations.** 'Selected locations' makes it a **Rollout**. Read every such statement against the 2×2 grid: *Big Bang* always means all locations, *Rollout* always means selected locations, and *Modular* always means selected modules.

items.q: **True or False:** In an ERP consolidation project, companies migrate from several ERPs to one.
items.explain: **True.** **Harmonization / Consolidation = reducing many instances or types of ERPs to one.** It usually follows mergers and acquisitions, and its hardest part is reconciling **conflicting master data** across the systems.

items.q: Which of the following is **not** part of the ERP implementation?
items.explain: **Customers.** The implementation involves **vendors** (who supply the package), **consultants** (who implement it) and **employees** (who use it and provide requirements). Customers are *affected by* the outcome but are not participants in the implementation itself.

items.q: Which of the following is **not** a myth of ERP?
options: ERP means more work and procedures
ERP is the sole responsibility of management
ERP integrates and automates business processes
items.explain: **'ERP integrates and automates business processes' is TRUE**, so it is not a myth. The other three are myths. Careful with the question's negative phrasing — it asks which statement is *not* false.

items.q: Which one of the following is part of the organization?
items.explain: **All of the above.** An enterprise is **a group of people with a common goal**, deploying **resources** to reach it. The word *common* is the operative one — Unit 1 is largely about what goes wrong when departments stop sharing that goal.

items.q: ERP supports __________ currency value.
items.explain: **Multiple.** This follows from the **'Multi' problems** of the modern enterprise — multi-country brings multi-currency, multi-lingual and multi-cultural along with it. A single-currency system is disqualified for any multinational.

items.q: The most important step of ERP implementation is _________.
items.explain: **Gap analysis.** It is where the difference between the **To-Be** process and what the package does out of the box is established — and therefore where the project's real cost is decided, since every gap must be **customized** (expensive, risky) or **absorbed by changing the business**.

items.q: An enterprise is a group of people with ________.
options: a separate goal for each department
items.explain: **A common goal.** Departmental goals that drift apart are precisely the problem — *Production → Quantity, Sales → Variety* — and enterprise-level planning is the fix.

items.q: The traditional business system is called a _________.
items.explain: **Legacy system.** Nestlé had **nine different general ledgers** and Agilent inherited **2,200 legacy applications** from HP — both were replaced by ERP.

items.q: _________ approach reduces data redundancy and provides up-to-date information.
items.explain: **Integrated data model.** This is driver **C** of **EPIC** — from departmental databases to one **company-wide integrated database**, whose three stated advantages are **no data duplication, data standardization and data tracking**.

items.q: The main drawback of a legacy system is ________.
items.explain: **No integration.** Note the drawback is *not* that legacy systems are old or slow — it is that **they do not talk to each other**, producing information silos: **D**uplication of data, **N**o integration, **S**ystems can't update online.

items.q: An ERP system is for _______.
items.explain: **The entire organization.** ERP *'attempts to integrate all departments and functions across a company onto a single computing system.'* Believing it is only for production is the misconception created by its **MRP → MRP II → ERP** manufacturing origins.

items.q: The cost of ERP ________.
items.explain: **All the above.** The cost has nine direct elements plus indirect ones, and licence cost alone scales with **user count and user type** (developers, professional users, ordinary users all priced differently).

items.q: The ASAP road-map is a detailed project plan by _______ that describes all activities in an implementation.
items.explain: **SAP** — the name literally contains it: **A**ccelerated **SAP**. Oracle's methodology is **AIM / Fast Forward**; PwC/IBM's is **Ascendant**; Scala/Epicor's is **Signature**.

items.q: The company should conduct a _________ about the implementation and implementation strategies.
items.explain: **Feasibility study.** It is a **Pre-Implementation** activity, listed as *'Feasibility / ROI / Business case'*, and it is what establishes whether the project should proceed at all.

items.q: The ERP implementation process has _______ phases.
items.explain: **Six** — *Papa Please Bring Rice For Supper*: **P**re-implementation, **P**roject preparation, **B**usiness blueprinting, **R**ealization, **F**inal preparation & go live, **S**upport.

items.q: In which phase are roles identified and responsibilities assigned?
items.explain: **Project planning / preparation.** Team selection, creating a proper structure, standards and governance, and the **project charter** all belong to this phase — the phase that decides *how the project will be run*.

items.q: The ________ team normally includes hired consultants and the in-house team.
items.explain: **All the above** — team selection is explicitly **'internal and external'**. Note the two distinct bodies formed in Pre-Implementation: the **steering committee** (senior, managerial) and the **implementation team** (technical, product expert).

items.q: In which phase is data conversion carried out?
items.explain: **Going live.** Realization produces only the **data / system migration *document***; the actual **data migration** is one of the ten final checks before cut-over. Agilent's worst damage came from exactly this step — *'converting backlog from legacy to new systems'*.

items.q: Name the phase in which the actual users of the system are given training on how to use it.
items.explain: **End user training**, in Final Preparation. Do not confuse it with **core team training**, which happens earlier in **Business Blueprinting** — the core team must understand the package before they can design the To-Be process on it.

items.q: _______ is the final phase in the ERP implementation life cycle.
items.explain: **Post implementation** — the **Support** phase. Remember the equation: **ERP Lifecycle = ERP Implementation Life cycle + ERP Support Life cycle**. Support is half the life cycle, not an epilogue.

items.q: ________ are the people who will be using the ERP system once it is deployed.
items.explain: **End-users.** Their involvement is listed as a defining feature of ERP adaptation, and their resistance is what turned into **rebellion** at Nestlé in 2000.

items.q: Most companies use ______ to help with the ERP implementation process.
items.explain: **Consultants.** Agilent used *roughly 100 Oracle consultants*, and in the sample cost table **consulting is the single largest line — 800 of 1,914 lakhs**. Since the software itself is a commodity, *'success solely depends on good implementation'*.
